content:
For \(n\ge 17\), look at the first \(17\) terms. Let

\[
A_i=\sum_{k=i}^{i+6} a_k<0 \quad (1\le i\le 11),
\]
\[
B_i=\sum_{k=i}^{i+10} a_k>0 \quad (1\le i\le 7).
\]

Then

\[
\sum_{i=1}^{11} A_i=\sum_{i=1}^{7} B_i,
\]

because each side gives the same weighted sum of \(a_1,\dots,a_{17}\), with coefficients

\[
1,2,3,4,5,6,7,7,7,7,7,6,5,4,3,2,1.
\]

But \(\sum A_i<0\) while \(\sum B_i>0\), a contradiction. Hence \(n\le 16\).

Now construct a sequence of length \(16\):

\[
5,5,-13,5,5,5,-13,5,5,-13,5,5,5,-13,5,5.
\]

This repeats the block \(5,5,-13,5,5,5,-13\), whose total sum is \(-1\). Every \(7\) consecutive terms sum to \(-1<0\). Every \(11\) consecutive terms consist of a full \(7\)-term block plus the next \(4\) terms, giving

\[
-1+2=1>0.
\]

So \(16\) terms are attainable.

\[
\boxed{16}
\]
